text:
ana: heads up — I hit a weird combo on Windows where `redwoodctl login` succeeds but `redwoodctl local test --profile=ci` inside the docker image reads an older token. Seems like we stored token in Windows Credential Manager and the localtest mount overlays a stale file.

drew: oof. We recently added credential helper support on Windows that writes to the Windows Credential Manager and also drops a token file for backward compatibility. If both exist the loader prefers cred helper by default, but when you mount $HOME/.redwoodctl into the container the file takes precedence. Bug is precedence flips depending on runtime.

mike: repro steps I used: 1) `redwoodctl login` on Windows, confirm cred-manager has entry. 2) create a different token file in $HOME/.redwoodctl/ci/token (older value). 3) run `redwoodctl local test --profile=ci --mount $HOME/.redwoodctl:/home/dev/.redwoodctl` and inside container `redwoodctl whoami` shows old user.

sasha: short term we should: 1) Change precedence to always prefer credential helper over mounted token when `--credential-helper` is enabled. 2) Add `redwoodctl doctor` subcommand that checks for dual-stores and reports stale token conflicts. 3) For localtest, add `--prefer-credhelper` flag so container can call back to host credential helper via a small socket proxy (opt-in).

ana: (typo) ana: I mean sasha's plan looks good. Also add telemetry event when we detect the mismatch so we can see how common it is.

drew: implementation note: credential helper on Windows is a separate process using https://github.com/docker-credential-helpers as pattern. We'll need a tiny shim that can be mounted into the container for CI/node environments. For now, `--prefer-credhelper=false` remains default for backwards compat.

mike: I'll pick up the doctor CLI + telemetry. PR branch: dev/doctor-cred-conflict. Will add unit tests simulating both stores.

sasha: I'll do the precedence change and add a warning when `local test` detects a mounted token that conflicts with the credential helper. Also add a short doc note in DevEx about credential helper interactions with local containers.

ci-bot: created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/3860 (labels: devex, cli, windows, cred-helper)

ana: thanks team. For anyone hitting this now: quick workaround is to remove stale files from $HOME/.redwoodctl or run `redwoodctl login --force-refresh` before starting local test.

drew: noted — will also add an exit code and clearer help text for `login --force-refresh` so CI scripts can call it safely.

ana: marking this thread resolved until PRs land. :white_check_mark:
